name: New Tab Tasks successor
demand: Search volume and a reliable total addressable market are unverified. The May 27, 2026 Chromium forum post lists New Tab Tasks at 28,000 users; another poster says almost 30,000 active users and 150+ positive reviews. These are forum claims, not independently confirmed store data: https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-extensions/c/m9V8BJOgTEg. A close free comparator, Taskade's New Tab Todo List, shows 30,000 Chrome Web Store users and 90 ratings, but its listing says it was last updated Dec 20, 2024: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/new-tab-todo-list-checkli/hdkbnhcgfcokjhlfiicbphafdnipnhjf. Broader demand is visible in Momentum's 2,000,000 store users and 13.7k ratings, though it is a wider dashboard product: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/momentum/laookkfknpbbblfpciffpaejjkokdgca?hl=en-GB&xs=1. These user counts do not establish paid conversion or revenue. No regulated buyer population identified.
prices: Momentum Plus is $39.95 USD/year; its free tier includes a to-do list: https://momentumdash.com/?trk=public_post-text. ReadyTab Pro is CHF 24.99/year or CHF 52.99 lifetime: https://www.readytab.cloud/index.html. Taskade's New Tab Todo List listing says it is free and describes Pro as a future option, without a price: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/new-tab-todo-list-checkli/hdkbnhcgfcokjhlfiicbphafdnipnhjf. Another new-tab task extension says its features are free, with subscription-based ad removal mentioned but no price: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/to-do-list-chrome-extensi/kpdfnfkfggloklhgakceaoleccfefhef. New Tab Tasks' own price and paid-plan details are unverified.

revenue_proof.claim: No verified product-specific payment count or revenue found. On May 27, 2026, AppBox's representative said a significant share of affected extensions' users were paying subscribers, but did not attribute a count or revenue to New Tab Tasks. The same post lists its 28,000 users; that is not revenue proof.

copy_speed: Fast and current competition is evident, although update dates do not always prove launch dates. TaskTab was created May 6, 2026 according to Chrome-Stats, and its official listing shows an update on May 11; it had 45 users and 1 rating on the opened listing: https://chrome-stats.com/d/koncbgionnhbemmefolgmcdaeneagmki and https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/tasktab-new-tab-for-googl/koncbgionnhbemmefolgmcdaeneagmki. ReadyTab's developer said it had just been published on June 12; its store listing shows an Aug 28 update, 80 users and 7 ratings: https://www.reddit.com/r/chrome_extensions/comments/1u42a24/build_my_personal_starter_tab/ and https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/readytab-new-tab-dashboar/ccakmoofmcbcplfaloecafdmpaihlenm. A task-focused new-tab listing updated Oct 1, 2026 shows 605 users and includes multiple lists and sync: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/to-do-list-chrome-extensi/kpdfnfkfggloklhgakceaoleccfefhef. Initial launch dates for the latter two TaskTab-like task listings are unverified.
platform_risk: High single-platform dependency. The AppBox representative alleged affected extensions, including New Tab Tasks, were removed under a generic Spam policy notice; on July 10, 2026, Chrome DevRel replied that Google had considered the extensions individually and believed enforcement was correct, without publicly specifying New Tab Tasks' particular violation: https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-extensions/c/m9V8BJOgTEg. Google's policies permit payment collection subject to conditions, while also requiring clear disclosures, limited data use and compliance with store policies: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/accepting-payment?authuser=9 and https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/policies. Manifest V3 requires extension logic to be included in the package, not remotely hosted: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/migrate/what-is-mv3. A paid tier is possible, but this specific removal episode makes store approval and monetization a material risk.
defensible_asset: No proprietary UK data, UK rules engine, or strong moat identified. Potential defensibility is habit, task history, and useful integrations, but competitors already offer sync, multiple lists, and integrations; ReadyTab also provides export and local-first storage: https://momentumdash.com/?trk=public_post-text, https://www.readytab.cloud/index.html, and https://www.readytab.cloud/privacy.html. Switching costs look low to moderate unless a distinctive integration or workflow earns daily use.
build_effort: Moderate for a focused Chrome-only, local-first new-tab task list: Chrome documents the new-tab override and extension storage APIs: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/ui/override-chrome-pages?authuser=370 and https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/storage?authuser=1. Built-in Chrome sync is limited to about 100 KB total and 8 KB per item, so larger histories or broader cross-browser sync may require a backend: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/storage?authuser=1. Multi-provider integrations, cloud sync, payment entitlements, privacy disclosures, and store review raise this to medium-high effort: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/policies.
channel: Use Chrome Web Store search/listing optimization, useful search-indexed help pages, and public launch or feedback posts only where community rules allow. Collect emails only through an explicit opt-in. ICO guidance treats private social-media DMs as electronic mail and says sole traders are protected like individuals for marketing email/text, so avoid cold email, SMS, WhatsApp, and DMs: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/key-concepts-for-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/ and https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; the <=5 hours/week constraint cannot be substantiated before operating the product. Keeping the first version local-first and narrow should reduce service work, but paid cloud sync and integrations add support and maintenance.
desk_test: Within one day, make a clickable mock and a simple opt-in page for the multi-list and sync proposition, with Momentum's published $39.95/year plan as a visible price benchmark: https://momentumdash.com/?trk=public_post-text. Share it only through a permitted public feedback channel, with no direct messages, and measure voluntary waitlist or paid-tier-interest clicks. This tests stated interest, not purchases or retention.
red_flags: Demand is supported by store-user proxies and the removed extension's forum-reported audience, but current paying-user demand and product revenue are unverified. Free competitors make willingness to pay uncertain. Google's July 2026 response means the removal cannot safely be dismissed as an AppBox-only mistake. Automation share and owner workload are also unverified; 0 in automation_share_pct means no verified percentage, not a claim that automation is actually zero.
